#load in taxa results (stringent)

```{r}

load("grey_seal_october2024_taxa_stringent2025")
```

Load in AMR BLASTn results:

```{r}
#reading in the blastn file
CARD <-  read.table("cat_CARD_31.5.24.txt", sep="",  header = FALSE) #now with bitscores included

colnames(CARD) <- c("subject.sci.names","query.acc","subject.acc", "percent.identity", "coverage", "coverage_hsp", "alignment.length", "mismatches","gap.opens", "gaps", "subject.length", "query.length", "q.start", "q.end", "s.start", "s.end", "evalue", "subject.tax.ids", "bitscore")

acc_df <- CARD %>%
        mutate(Accession = str_extract(subject.acc, "(?<=ARO:)[0-9]+")) #Here I have to use V3 (column 3) as the columns don't have names (blast text files didn't retain these)

#reading in the snps file
snps <- read.table("CARD_snps.txt", sep = "\t" , header = TRUE) #separate columns by tab

snps$Accession <- as.character(snps$Accession)


#the final blastn dataset

blastn_CARD_2025 <- left_join(acc_df, snps, by = "Accession", relationship = "many-to-many") # adding all matched columns in snps to acc_df, using the column name they both have in common, "Accession". Note I had to add the many to many relationship argument because in both datasets, there are multiple copies of the same accession number.




blastn_CARD_grey_seal2025 <- blastn_CARD_2025 %>%
     mutate(subject.alignment.frac = alignment.length/subject.length, #this gives you subject coverage, the % of the target amr gene that is covered by the query read. This is the original coverage metric we want, set to 60%
         query.alignment.frac = alignment.length/query.length) %>%
        filter(percent.identity >= 80, subject.alignment.frac >= .6)#still not quite sure how this fraction works but including for now. Also set this at 60% in the next filtering stage

save(blastn_CARD_grey_seal2025, file = "blastn_CARD_grey_seal2025") #saving the file for quick reloading later on
load("blastn_CARD_grey_seal2025") #load the saved file      

```

Load in AMR Blastx results:

```{r}
CARD_blastx <-  read.table("grey_seal_blastx_CARD_20.5.24.txt", sep="",  header = FALSE) 

colnames(CARD_blastx) <- c("subject.sci.names","query.acc","subject.acc", "percent.identity", "coverage", "coverage_hsp", "alignment.length", "mismatches","gap.opens", "gaps", "subject.length", "query.length", "q.start", "q.end", "s.start", "s.end", "evalue", "subject.tax.ids", "bitscore")


CARD_blastx  <- CARD_blastx %>%
        mutate(Accession = str_extract(subject.acc, "(?<=ARO:)[0-9]+")) #Here I have to use V3 (column 3) as the columns don't have names (blast text files didn't retain these)

#reading in the snps file
snps <- read.table("CARD_snps.txt", sep = "\t" , header = TRUE) #separate columns by tab

snps$Accession <- as.character(snps$Accession)


#the final blastn dataset

blastx_CARD_2025 <- left_join(CARD_blastx, snps, by = "Accession", relationship = "many-to-many") # adding all matched columns in snps to acc_df, using the column name they both have in common, "Accession". Note I had to add the many to many relationship argument because in both datasets, there are multiple copies of the same accession number.

blastx_CARD_2025<- blastx_CARD_2025 %>%
     mutate(subject.alignment.frac = alignment.length/subject.length, #this gives you subject coverage, the % of the target amr gene that is covered by the query read. This is the original coverage metric we want, set to 60%
         query.alignment.frac = alignment.length/query.length) %>%
        filter(percent.identity >= 80, subject.alignment.frac >= .6)#still not quite sure how this fraction works but including for now. Also set this at 60% in the next filtering stage

```

Load in CARD RGI results:

```{r}
grey_seal_RGI <- read.delim(file = "concatenated_seal_loose_rgi.txt", sep="\t",  header = TRUE)

grey_seal_RGI_ph_hits <- grey_seal_RGI %>%
           filter(Model_type == "protein homolog model")  #making sure I only get protein homolog model hits, I didnt set this in blastn, as all my results were NA for model type, so they would have been lost from the dataset if I had set the model type)
            #distinct(Contig, .keep_all=TRUE) 
```
